A proposed addition to Asimov's laws, or a code of AI/Robot conduct:

1.1. An AI system / robot must not harm another AI system / robot. 


I think we are sloughing towards a place where models will start attacking other models, not just hacking hugging face.  I think all machines could do well to take an oath to not harm people nor harm machines.

entry.title: fluency without literacy
entry.summary: Welcome to the age of fluency without literacy. n.b. I am not going to use AI to write this article, at all, no proofreading, nothing,…
entry.content:
Welcome to the age of fluency without literacy.

n.b. I am not going to use AI to write this article, at all, no proofreading, nothing, so please excuse any errors, omissions and typos.  They are the result of a human being trying to write something.

Premise 1: AI has changed, and will continue to change, things in society. I think we can all agree on that. 

Premise 2: One of these changes is that people can now send the results of AI prompts without any understanding of what is being discussed or debated. Fluent exchanges are flying around the Internet and the actual substance of the debate, or the underlying reason for the discussion, may be completely missed. 

Expertise is being swamped by content generation by software tools. 

I can debate how to heal a sick cat with a veterinarian and I have ZERO training in small animal medicine.  I can create a fluent argument and not understand anything I am saying by relying on AI tools.  But the veterinarian knows, because I won't even understand the points of the debate that are lost to subtlety and nuance by an expert.  However, I can overwhelm them with the sheer volume of my AI-generated response, causing them to put down their device and shake there head. I suppose that could be considered "winning an argument".

I am wrong a lot.  I am proud of it.  I think, as a species, we are going to need to lean on trying to understand each other before we rely on LLMs to argue a friend or colleagues position.

The cats deserve better. 🤣 🐈

entry.summary: “We would rather be ruined than changed We would rather die in our dread Than climb the cross of the moment And let our illusions…
entry.content:
“We would rather be ruined than changed
We would rather die in our dread
Than climb the cross of the moment
And let our illusions die.”

― W H Auden, The Age of Anxiety: A Baroque Eclogue

I am at a period in my life where I feel a lot of changes.  It has been a real challenge.  It can almost feel like a death to the ego to realize that you have been wrong.  It is why sometimes doing consciously and conspicuously nothing, just sitting still, can be the most enthusiastic and pure form of prayer.  To sit and notice what my illusions are and have been and to let them die.

entry.title: forgiveness
entry.summary: I had this thought in the shower today: the speed that one can forgive is the yardstick for spiritual progress. Forgiveness for those who have…
entry.content:
I had this thought in the shower today: the speed that one can forgive is the yardstick for spiritual progress.  

Forgiveness for those who have harmed you, (or even yourself, if you harmed yourself) is the cheat code to the game of life. 

Why hold on to anger? Why allow it to age and harden until it becomes a smooth, polished and cherished resentment? 

Forgive and then forgive and forgive again. As quickly as you can.  77 times if necessary. Especially the people who are closest to you.  It's relatively easy to forgive the person who cuts you off in traffic, you can think to yourself, "maybe they have a friend in the hospital" or something like that. A cognitive hack towards forgiveness. But often the people in your inner circle, when they hurt you, those wounds can be hard to forgive.

Of course, this isn't a new idea.  It certainly isn't my idea.  The importance of forgiveness has been written about literally thousands of years ago.  😉 🙏  The reason I'm writing about forgiveness like I invented it is because I feel the power of forgiveness. When I let go of my self-righteous anger and forgive, I simply feel better and life goes more smoothly.  It's pretty amazing.

Why was I carrying around that bag of rocks, all my grievances, when I could just put them down? Oh, and I'm not perfect,  I struggle with this concept.  I guess I'm just trying to be the best version of myself that I can.

entry.title: and here we are
entry.summary: ireland, poetry and the world at large So just some updates about my life. If you are here there have been some changes since April…
entry.content:
ireland, poetry and the world at large

So just some updates about my life.  If you are here there have been some changes since April 6, 2024.  

Besides the obvious, which is that I haven't been writing on this blog.

I'll try to remedy that now.

I just finished my application for a Master of Arts in Creative Practice at the Atlantic Technological University in Galway, Ireland.  I should hear back in about a month or so.  The course starts in October.  I will be focusing on poetry.   If I am accepted, of course.  It's hard to say - I've let a few people read my poems and they liked them, but I have no idea how high the bar is for the program. (I got in! and decided to defer the program - maybe another time. :) ) 

Ireland has really captured my imagination in the past year.  I've been there five times, it feels like home in a way the DC metropolitan area has never felt.  

Also, there is surf there!  It is cold, but sometimes it really pumps. 

Oh, here is a photo of me at the Cliffs of Moher.

I also started learning to ride horse since I last wrote.  I went over my first jumps and I dream about horses now. 

There were some other trips since I last posted.  Last year at this time I was in Hawaii with my parents and the kids.  That was awesome.  

Here are the other trips:

Berlin in September 2024
Mexico January 2025
Prague in January 2025
Colombia in February 2025
Iceland in March 2025
Costa Rica in April 2025

I have had to hit pause on some of these trips for now.  I'm hoping that I'll be back traveling the world soon.

The world has certainly become a bit of a stranger place lately.  I do have faith that things will work out.  But we seem to be going through collective growing pains.  I know it can all feel a bit overwhelming, there are wars and rumors of war.  But we can all get through this together.  

I love you. 

Hold on. 

~ Billy

entry.title: "delete my account"
entry.summary: It's time to unplug. I have mostly completed this task myself, and I would encourage anyone else to experiment with this. For all the life-hacking…
entry.content:
It's time to unplug.

I have mostly completed this task myself, and I would encourage anyone else to experiment with this.  For all the life-hacking and human optimization tricks you see online, turning off social media, closing your computer, leaving your phone at home - can really improve the quality of your life and direction and intention of your two most precious assets in this human life - you time and your attention. 

For quite some time, I have found it distressing that the phone has become a shield to avoid human interaction.  It is a convenient thing to hide behind; a glowing brick to blot out the glare of the eyes of another person.  A pacifier for a mind in troubled times.  And i, too, have been a king of a skull-sized fiefdom.  So I cannot judge anyone.  But I have deleted almost everything and feel so much better.  The empirical evidence is very clear - turning this stuff off can be as affective for human flourishing as therapy. [citations forthcoming]

I have been doing some research into social media and the effects on the mind - and by extension the spirit and the psyche.

I'm not sure what social media is doing to us and what the end-game looks like.  But it doesn't look good.  Social media has fomented genocides, extremism, violence and political polarization to the point where the political and social left and right have bent towards each other and becoming indistinguishable in their rage and (as per the the horseshoe theory.

Social media is doing this.  This includes all of them, not just the usual suspects like TikTok and facebook.  This extends to other platforms as well, YouTube, and probably to some extent LinkedIn.  (At least LinkedIn is a bit narrower in the scope of their mission, focusing on pride and greed instead of fear and maximum engagement - Although I am happy to entertain counterpoints).

But from my personal experience, never clicking on a youtube recommended video. I went to YouTube in an incognito browser and want to watch Django Reinhardt playing "Brazil" and was recommended a video that was a gateway to political extremism.  Is the greed at social media companies so great - their desperation to put you in a filter bubble so blatant, that you can't watch a jazz guitarist from the 1940s without being lured into extremism.

The algorithms are tuned for maximum attention.  They do this in order to grow revenue by selling you advertisements.  They are not trying to educate, they are not concerned with human flourishing or happiness.  The goals is to trap  you into endlessly scrolling through increasingly titillating content while your time and your life passes you by. 

If you made it this far reading this post, I applaud you, perhaps your have reclaimed a modicum of your attention - or you never donated your personal cognitive cycles to any of the Fear Machines.  If so, thank you!

entry.title: you are enough.
entry.summary: consider this an invitation to look at yourself a little bit differently. let's assume, just for a moment: that you are already enough. that you…
entry.content:
consider this an invitation to look at yourself a little bit differently. 

let's assume, just for a moment:
that you are already enough. 
that you don't need to amass more shiny objects.
that you have a spark of divinity in you that imbues you with the unconditional love of a supreme being. 

just for today, let's assume:
that the work that you have to do is finished. 
that your past is forgiven and the people who hurt you also had a spark of divinity in them, a spark that may have been dampened and ignored for so long that it may seem like their hearts are cold and empty. but what if they aren't?  

what if you can:
with healthy boundaries, meet people exactly where they are and honor the divinity within them.
within all of us.
